description: Curated MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise technique catalogue for SentinelForge AI Phase 1. Catalogue entries are reference inventory only — catalogue membership is NOT implemented detection coverage.

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown or when password hashes are obtained.
entries.mapping_rationale: Parent-level coverage for T1110.001 (Password Guessing) and T1110.003 (Password Spraying). The FailedLoginBurstRule and PasswordSprayRule implement the sub-techniques; T1110 itself has no independent detection beyond its sub-techniques.
investigation_recommendations: Check for successful logins from source IP

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may guess passwords to attempt access to accounts without prior knowledge of legitimate credentials.
entries.mapping_rationale: Multiple failed authentication attempts against one account within a time window is the exact definition of password guessing against live authentication.
investigation_recommendations: Check for successful logins from source IP
Force password reset for targeted accounts

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may use a single or small list of commonly used passwords against many different accounts to attempt to acquire valid account credentials.
entries.mapping_rationale: One source IP attempting authentication against multiple distinct usernames is the exact definition of password spraying. The PasswordSprayRule groups failures by source IP and counts distinct target usernames.
investigation_recommendations: Check for successful logins from source IP against targeted accounts
Force password reset for targeted accounts

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may attempt to obtain plaintext passwords from password hashes obtained from credential stores.
entries.mapping_rationale: No file content access or hash extraction telemetry is available in the normalized schema.
investigation_recommendations: Review file access events on credential store locations
Monitor for password cracking tool execution

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may use credentials obtained from previous breaches to attempt access to accounts.
entries.mapping_rationale: Authentication failures against many accounts from one source could indicate credential stuffing, but the current PasswordSprayRule detects spraying (one password vs many users), not stuffing (many known credentials vs one/many users). No dedicated rule exists.
investigation_recommendations: Check for successful logins from source IP

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may acquire credentials from password stores such as password managers or browser credential databases.
entries.mapping_rationale: No file access monitoring or credential store telemetry is available in the normalized schema.
investigation_recommendations: Monitor file access on password manager databases
Review process execution for credential dumping tools

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries.
entries.mapping_rationale: Parent-level coverage for T1059.001 (PowerShell). The SuspiciousPowerShellRule implements the sub-technique; T1059 itself has no independent detection beyond its sub-technique.
investigation_recommendations: Isolate host if command is malicious

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution.
entries.mapping_rationale: PowerShell process execution with suspicious indicators (encoded command, execution policy bypass, download-and-execute) is consistent with T1059.001, but benign administrative PowerShell usage can also contain encoded commands.
investigation_recommendations: Isolate host if command is malicious

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may abuse the Windows command shell for execution.
entries.mapping_rationale: cmd.exe process execution is observable via Sysmon Event ID 1, but no detection rule exists for Windows Command Shell usage. Normal command shell use is common and requires careful threshold tuning.
investigation_recommendations: Review command line content for suspicious patterns
Correlate with file system and network activity

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may abuse Unix shell commands and scripts for execution.
entries.mapping_rationale: Linux auth logs capture authentication outcomes but not process execution or command line data.
investigation_recommendations: Implement process execution monitoring on Linux hosts

entries.technique_description: An adversary may rely upon specific actions by a user in order to gain execution.
entries.mapping_rationale: Parent-level coverage for T1204.002 (Malicious File). The SuspiciousProcessTreeRule implements the sub-technique conditionally (when correlated file activity exists); T1204 itself has no independent detection beyond its sub-technique.
investigation_recommendations: Check email attachments and web downloads

entries.technique_description: An adversary may rely upon a user opening a malicious file in order to gain execution.
entries.mapping_rationale: Parent-child process correlation (Office → PowerShell) plus correlated file activity can indicate malicious file execution. The SuspiciousProcessTreeRule maps T1204.002 when correlated file activity (create/download/open) exists on the same host/user within the time window.
investigation_recommendations: Check email attachments and web downloads

entries.technique_description: An adversary may rely upon a user clicking a malicious link in order to gain execution.
entries.mapping_rationale: No web proxy, browser telemetry, or file download monitoring is available in the normalized schema.
investigation_recommendations: Review web proxy logs for malicious URL access
Correlate with process execution on user workstations

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols to avoid detection.
entries.mapping_rationale: Periodic outbound connections with non-standard ports and suspicious process context are consistent with C2 beaconing, but legitimate periodic traffic (EDR heartbeats, software updates) can produce identical patterns. T1071 is only mapped when protocol-specific C2 context is present.
investigation_recommendations: Correlate with process execution events on source host

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may communicate using web protocols (HTTP/HTTPS) to avoid detection.
entries.mapping_rationale: HTTP/HTTPS connections are observable via Sysmon Event ID 3, but standard port 443 connections are explicitly excluded from T1071 mapping by C2BeaconRule. No web proxy telemetry is available.
investigation_recommendations: Check destination reputation for HTTPS connections
Review process context for unusual HTTPS usage

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may attempt to gather information about services running on hosts.
entries.mapping_rationale: Network connection data is available via Sysmon Event ID 3, but no detection rule correlates individual connections into scanning patterns.
investigation_recommendations: Review outbound connection patterns from hosts
Identify hosts connecting to many different ports

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may attempt to gather information about accounts on a system or domain.
entries.mapping_rationale: Authentication events reveal usernames but not account enumeration activity. No process command line monitoring on Linux is available.
investigation_recommendations: Review authentication patterns for unusual username enumeration

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of bypassing access controls.
entries.mapping_rationale: Successful authentication with valid credentials is observable, but distinguishing legitimate use from compromised credential use requires additional context not available in current telemetry.
investigation_recommendations: Check for logins at unusual times or from unusual locations
Review successful logins from new source IPs

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may configure system mechanisms to automatically execute programs during boot or logon.
entries.mapping_rationale: No registry monitoring or boot-time process telemetry is available in the normalized schema.
investigation_recommendations: Implement registry monitoring for autostart keys
Review startup folder and scheduled tasks

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may use Registry Run keys to establish persistence.
entries.mapping_rationale: No registry monitoring is available in the normalized schema.
investigation_recommendations: Implement registry monitoring for Run keys

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to log into remote services.
entries.mapping_rationale: SSH and RDP connection attempts are observable via network and auth telemetry, but no detection rule correlates them into lateral movement detection.
investigation_recommendations: Review remote access patterns from user workstations

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may use SSH to move laterally through an environment.
entries.mapping_rationale: SSH connections on port 22 are observable via network connection and authentication telemetry, but no detection rule exists for SSH lateral movement.

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may gather data from local systems.
entries.mapping_rationale: Process command lines are observable, but file create monitoring beyond Sysmon Event ID 11 is not used by any detection rule.
investigation_recommendations: Review file access patterns on sensitive directories

entries.technique_description: Adversaries may exfiltrate data over the C2 channel.
entries.mapping_rationale: Network connection data is available but outbound data volume monitoring is not, making exfiltration detection impossible with current telemetry.
investigation_recommendations: Review large data transfers to external destinations

Review service and process termination events
